raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #42528.

`TreeSpeculativeSamplingTargetOnly` draws coins from `[0, 1)` and, after rejecting a draft, samples the bonus/replacement token from the residual `relu(target - draft)`. The residual can be **empty**: every token the target gives mass to was a rejected draft (the kernel copies `target` into `draft` for each rejected token, so `q - p == 0` there). The easiest way to hit this in practice is a renormalized one-token nucleus (`top_k` + `top_p`): its probability is `1 - 2^-24`, not `1.0`, and `torch.rand` returns exactly `1 - 2^-24` with probability `2^-24`. The half-open CDF test (`coin < prob_acc`, #35798) then rejects the only token with target mass, `sum(relu(q - p)) == 0`, `u == 0`, no bucket is ever selected and the fallback emits token id `d - 1` — a token with zero target probability.

With MTP on a 248k vocabulary this shows up as a rare garbage token (id `vocab_size - 1`) in the middle of a generation.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/speculative/sampling.cuh` (shared device header, so the CUDA/ROCm JIT launchers and the MUSA AOT build all pick it up): also accumulate `sum(q)` in the first pass; when `sum(relu(q - p))` is not `> 0`, sample from the target distribution itself (`u = coin * sum(q)`, buckets from `q`). The acceptance test is unchanged, so #35798's semantics (half-open CDF, no zero-mass drafts) are preserved.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_speculative_sampling.py`: add `upper-endpoint-empty-residual` — target `[0, 1 - 2^-24, 0]`, draft token 1, coin `1 - 2^-24`: the draft is rejected (`accept_token_num == 0`) and the emitted token must be `1`, not `2`.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_speculative_sampling.py`: `8 passed` with the fix (1-GPU, JIT build). On `main` (`660b17e8dc`) the new `upper-endpoint-empty-residual` case fails (`predicts[0] == 2`, i.e. `vocab_size - 1`) and the other 7, including #35798's `interior-boundary` and both endpoints, pass — so the acceptance semantics are untouched.
- Minimal reproduction from #42528 (248,320-token vocabulary, one-token nucleus renormalized to `0.99999994`, 8 rows, coin `0.99999994`): before, 8/8 rows accept 0 drafts and emit `248319`; after, 8/8 rows still accept 0 drafts (the draft is rejected by the half-open test, as before) and emit the nucleus token `1174`. `coin=0.5` is unchanged (3 drafts accepted per row).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No documentation change needed.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Kernel-level change on the rejection fallback path only; no end-to-end benchmark.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body: Hi maintainers — this PR has been open since 10-07 with the CI gate waiting on the `run-ci` label (pr-gate: `Require run-ci: true`). Could someone add the label (or point me at anything to change first)? Summary: when the rejection residual in `TreeSpeculativeSamplingTargetOnly` is empty, sample from the target distribution instead of emitting an out-of-range token (fixes #42528; unit test included, verified on a GB10 / DGX Spark box). Thanks!

Thanks @akatsukiwork0320 — agreed, the extra target reduction on the common paths was unnecessary. Pushed 2792e43: `sum_q` is now computed only inside the `residual_empty` branch (which is block-uniform because the residual sum is broadcast from `block_aggregate` before the branch), so the nonempty-residual and bonus paths are back to a single BlockReduce per tile; the empty-residual fallback semantics are unchanged. Verified locally on a GB10 (SM121): `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_speculative_sampling.py` 8/8 passed with the JIT kernel rebuilt from this header.
Thanks for the quick update and for testing on GB10. Moving the target reduction into the empty-residual branch addresses the issue I raised.

Status update for maintainers: the review comment from @akatsukiwork0320 has been addressed in 2792e43 (`sum_q` is now computed only inside the empty-residual branch; the common and bonus paths are unchanged) and they confirmed it. On the branch the kernel JIT-rebuilds cleanly and `test_speculative_sampling.py` passes on a GB10 (sm_121) box. The only failing checks are `pr-gate` (`Require run-ci: true`) and the `*-finish` aggregators that depend on it — no test job has run yet. Could a maintainer add the `run-ci` label and take a look? Happy to rebase or split if you prefer a different shape. Thanks!
